name: Tune Advisor Apply
rationale:
The Tune Advisor's Save writes its suggested changes to the FC. Pins
what reaches the FC: only the advised fields change, and nothing is
written unless every read is complete (a short reply would decode as a
tune of zeros), the FC still holds the tune the flights were flown on
(same values and profiles) and the model is disarmed; a failed write is
never committed to EEPROM; F is never applied without its rates (a
percentage-only rates_type applies neither); advice that would leave a
setting's range is not offered; a full-stick rate cut is one 20% step;
P is raised at most 50% above the pilot's own P (from changes.csv);
each stage is shown; a shaking axis that gets no P step still names the shake in its reasons (issue #2643); advice refreshes when the PID profile changes on the same aircraft. Issues #2639, #2640 and #2642: with polar cyclic on, roll gets no rate or F advice; a cyclic ring below 100% caps the rate asked at full stick; an axis that I-term relax does not act on gets no cut-off advice; and Apply refuses a flight whose Cyclic polarity, ring or I-term relax type differs from the FC. Issue #2808: the FC writes into whichever profile is active when each write arrives, so Apply asks MSP_STATUS for the active PID and rate profile before the reads, before each write, before the EEPROM commit and after the read-back; a switch before the first write changes nothing, a switch between writes stops before the next write and the commit, and a switch during the read-back is reported as unconfirmed. Each write leaves the MSP queue once (maxRetries = 0) and is resent by the page after a fresh profile check, so a lost reply's resend cannot land on a profile selected since the check; the resends are bounded at 6 attempts. The outcome dialog opens after the page is refocused, not before: a focus call made while it is open moved focus behind it, and on a radio without a touch screen (X14) its OK could not be reached. Issue #2788: the F rule had no overall bound, so accepted steps could take F and the rates it moves arbitrarily far from the pilot's own values. F, and the rates an F step moves, now stay within 3/5 to 5/3 of the pilot's own values (followed back through changes.csv as for P); past that no F step is given and the reasons say how far it already is, while a step back toward the pilot's own value is always given. Checked: F held past 60%, an F step within the bound, a step back toward the own value, and rates held past 167%. Issue #2829: a failed EEPROM commit after every write went through is reported as a save not confirmed whose changes may already be stored, never as nothing saved: the commit's answer can be lost after the FC stored the values, and an FC armed at the commit refuses it but marks the config dirty and stores it at the disarm. Checked disarmed and armed at the commit.
